{{Short description|Swiss mathematician (1801–1859)}}
[[File:Joseph Ludwig Raabe (1801–1859) by Carl Friedrich Irminger (1813–1863) ZBZ (A).jpg|thumb|Portrait by [[Carl Friedrich Irminger]], c. 1850]]  
'''Joseph Ludwig Raabe''' (15 May 1801 – 22 January 1859) was a Swiss [[mathematician]] best known for [[Raabe's ratio test]].<ref name="mg">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Raabe}}</ref>

==Life==
Raabe was born on 15 May 1801 into a Jewish family in [[Brody]], [[Austrian Galicia]] (now in [[Ukraine]]).<ref name=HDS>{{HDS|31631|author=Neuenschwander, Erwin|date=25 June 2012}}</ref> He was the son of Haja and Wolf Raabe, a writer and small businessman.<ref name=HDS/> As his parents were quite poor, Raabe was forced to earn his living from a very early age by giving private lessons.<ref name=HDS/> He studied mathematics at the [[Imperial-Royal Polytechnic Institute]] in [[Vienna]] from 1821 until 1827, the year he converted to Catholicism.<ref name=HDS/> 

Encouraged by Swiss mathematician {{ill|Johannes Eschmann|de|Johannes Eschmann (Geodät)}}, Raabe moved to [[Zürich]] in the autumn of 1831, where he became professor of mathematics at the ''[[Gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]]'' and ''[[Privatdozent]]'' at the [[University of Zürich]] in 1833.<ref name=HDS/> He was appointed associate professor at the university in 1843 and full professor in 1855.<ref name=HDS/> Rabbe became professor at the newly founded Swiss Polytechnicum (now [[ETH Zurich]]) in 1855.<ref name="mg"/> 

Raabe acquired the [[Swiss bourgeoisie|bourgeoisie]] of [[Schwamendingen]]-[[Oerlikon (Zurich)|Oerlikon]] in 1836 and received a ''doctor honoris causa'' from the University of Zürich in 1846.<ref name=HDS/> He died on 12 January 1859 in Zürich, aged 57.<ref name=HDS/>

==Work==
Raabe published works on [[definite integrals]], [[Bernoulli numbers]] and [[Series (mathematics)|series theory]].<ref name=HDS/> He is best known for [[Raabe's ratio test]], an extension of [[d'Alembert's ratio test]]. Raabe's test serves to determine the [[Convergent series|convergence]] or [[Divergent series|divergence]] of an infinite [[series (mathematics)|series]], in some cases.<ref name="mg"/> He is also known for the Raabe integral of the [[gamma function]]:<ref>{{citation|title=Elements of Mathematics Functions of a Real Variable|first=N.|last=Bourbaki|authorlink=Nicolas Bourbaki|publisher=Springer|year=2004|isbn=9783642593154|page=318|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=N-glBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA318}}.</ref>
:<math>\int_a^{a+1}\log\Gamma(t)\, dt = \tfrac{1}{2}\log 2\pi + a\log a - a,\quad a\ge0.</math>

==Publications==

* ''Differential- und Integralrechnung'' (3 volumes) (Zürich, 1839–1847)
* ''Mathematische Mitteilungen'' (2 volumes) (1857-1858)
